key_insight: Coupling CFD with DDA reveals that UV scattering inside airborne saliva droplets is highly non-uniform and materially changes predicted virus inactivation.
engineering_relevance: The model can improve the design and optimization of UV air purification systems by accounting for droplet physics that simpler inactivation laws miss.
method: 3D Euler-Lagrange CFD tracks droplet evaporation, transport, and interactions with airflow and walls.
DDA computes UV scattering for both spherical and irregular saliva droplets.
A new Dbouk-Yurkin inactivation law extends Chick-Watson to include scattering effects.
evidence_signal: The framework evaluates effects of droplet size distribution, concentration, airflow rate, and droplet-wall interactions on surviving coronavirus copies Ns under specified temperature, humidity, and virion size assumptions.
watch_item: Results depend on modeled assumptions and parameters, so real-world validation for different droplet compositions, virus loads, and UV setups remains important.
paper_title: An Innovative Computational Fluid Dynamics Discrete Dipole Approximation (CFD-DDA) Platform for Predicting Airborne Virus-in-Saliva Disinfection by Ultraviolet Irradiation
